# DOC006 dangling-citation

A prose citation such as `tickets.md section 6` or `tickets.md#lifecycle` names a file, section or anchor that does not exist.

## What it does

Scans the prose of tracked markdown under `docs/` and `notes/` and the comments of Rust files under `crates/` for a markdown file name followed by `section N` (also `sec`, or the section sign, with `N` like `6` or `6.2`) or by `#anchor`. The cited file is looked up beside the citing file, from the repo root, under `docs/`, and by path suffix. A section matches a numbered heading (`## 6. Title`, `### 6.2 Title`, `## Section 6`); an anchor matches a GitHub-style heading slug (duplicates numbered `-1`, `-2`), a `{#id}` suffix or an `<a id>` tag, ignoring case. The finding names the citation and what is missing.

Bare file mentions, fenced code blocks, URLs, markdown links (`DOC002` covers those), globs, generated pages and `historical` or superseded documents are not checked.

A missing target is followed through `docs/MOVED.toml` before it is reported. The `[moved]` table maps an old place to its new one; keys are `old.md`, `old.md#anchor` or `old.md section N`, values the same forms, optionally prefixed `merged:`. A bare file row carries the cited section or anchor over to the new file. Values prefixed `removed:` or `archive:` accept every citation of the key. Up to four rows are followed, and a row whose new place does not exist is itself reported. A missing `MOVED.toml` means no remaps; one that does not parse is a finding on the file.

## Why it matters

After documents are merged or renumbered, prose that says "see tickets.md section 6" silently points nowhere, and the reader cannot tell a stale pointer from a real one.

## Remedy

Fix the citation, or add a row to `docs/MOVED.toml` when the target moved.

## Examples

### A section that does not exist fires

```markdown expect=fire file=docs/design/a.md
# A

See tickets.md section 6 for the lifecycle. <!-- warn: DOC006 -->
```

```markdown file=docs/design/tickets.md
# Tickets

## 1. Intro
```

### A file that does not exist fires

```markdown expect=fire file=docs/design/a.md
# A

See gone.md#intro for details. <!-- warn: DOC006 -->
```

### A section that exists is clean

```markdown expect=clean file=docs/design/a.md
# A

See tickets.md section 1 for the lifecycle.
```

```markdown file=docs/design/tickets.md
# Tickets

## 1. Intro
```

### A citation inside a code fence is clean

````markdown expect=clean file=docs/design/a.md
# A

```
tickets.md section 6
```
````
